html:
SMTO-SCH-0004 — SMTO couldn't understand the schedule's date and time

GUID: 7fabb79a-e8f0-4caa-9453-98c5511c8cb8
Slug: schedule-next-run-at-must-be-an-iso
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • The date and time given for this schedule isn't in a form SMTO can read, or it names a date that doesn't exist. The schedule wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the schedule editor, fill in both the Starts date and the At time using the pickers, instead of typing them by hand. The pickers always produce a date and time SMTO can read.
  2. Check that the date really exists, for example not February 30 or April 31. An impossible date can't be turned into a run time.
  3. If you asked SMTO in a message, ask again with a full date and time, for example "October 9, 2026 at 2:30 PM". A complete date and time leaves nothing for SMTO to guess.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and the Schedules page shows the next run at the date and time you meant.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and include the date and time you entered. Don't resubmit the same value unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • next_run_at could not be parsed as an ISO 8601 date-time (malformed value, impossible date, invalid offset, or a date with no clock time).

What this means

  • The schedule time could not be parsed as an ISO date and time. A missing clock time, impossible date or malformed offset can fail this check. Time-zone lookup and daylight-saving ambiguity have separate diagnostics.

Why this can happen

  • The timestamp is incomplete or invalid for the supported ISO parser.

How to diagnose it

  • Check that next_run_at includes a real calendar date and a clock time. If an offset is supplied, verify its format and intended sign.

How to fix it

  • Send next_run_at as a full ISO 8601 date-time, such as 2026-10-09T14:30:00-07:00, with the intended date and offset. datetime.fromisoformat failed in events/timing.py resolve_at; date-only input is also wrapped into this error. Time-zone lookup and DST ambiguity are reported separately.
  • Enter a full ISO date and time, such as 2026-10-09T14:30:00-07:00, using the date and offset intended for the schedule.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The schedule preview resolves to the intended instant.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • fromisoformat parsing failed, including date-only input rejected by the wrapper.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
